Whether it’s knowing how to bypass TSA and customs quicker, battling jet lag or getting a free hotel upgrade, globetrotters know the ins and outs of being on the road and in the air.
After speaking to expert travelers, here are several strategies they recommend that can help other frequent flyers survive this type of lifestyle.
If you’re on a plane several times a year, and you hate waiting in those long lines at customs and/or airport security (where you find yourself packing and unpacking not only your suitcase but also yourself), then we recommend signing up for Global Entry (for those who often fly internationally), and TSA PreCheck.
Global Entry allows you to fly right through customs when you come back into the U.S. Rather than waiting in line, you check yourself in via an automated kiosk. Meanwhile, TSA PreCheck allows you to quickly pass through airport security without having to take anything off or take items out of your bag(s). The cost of signing up for Global Entry is US$100, which is valid for five years (if you have a Platinum AMEX, it’s $0). By signing up for Global Entry, you are automatically eligible for TSA PreCheck, for free.
If you don’t fly internationally often, then you can opt to sign up for TSA PreCheck alone for US$85, which is valid for five years. If you ask us, it’s better to just pay the additional $15 and get both. Because who knows, you may find yourself heading on a few international trips within the next five years, and that extra time saved can make all the difference!
At times, non-stop and direct flights are misunderstood as being one and the same, but they are completely different. A direct flight may still stop, but rather than switching planes like you would on a layover, you would just stay seated on the plane. On the other hand, a non-stop flight doesn’t stop at all until it reaches its final destination. As such, frequent travelers recommend that it’s best to choose non-stop rather than direct to save you time—those extra 2 or maybe even 3 hours of free time will be well worth it!
Traveling often means that soreness and stiffness come hand-in-hand. Sitting for several hours in an airplane seat is not ideal, so to combat tension and possible pain, bring a few tennis balls on the plane with you. Best way to use them is by rolling them under your feet and your thighs to keep stiffness at bay.
Traveling, regardless if it’s across the country or across the world, can take a toll on your mind and body. That’s why it’s important to find the right cure for jet lag—everyone is different and what works for one doesn’t necessarily work for another. For the best tips, check out our blog on How to beat jet lag when traveling domestically or internationally.
When business is slow, the concierge is known to upgrade guests to better rooms for free as long as they ask the front desk politely (and as long as there are not many other people around).
Before asking, double check to make sure that the hotel is, in fact, not full. You can either call and ask beforehand or check online on the hotel’s website to see how many rooms are still available.
If you’re a frequent flyer with tips that you can share with us (and everyone else), please comment below! We would love to hear what secrets you’ve learned while on the road and in the air. context:362 keywords: traveling, frequent travelers, customs, airport, TSA, TSA PreCheck, Global Entry, jet lag, non-stop, concierge, hotel, travel tips tags: travel planning, new context

content:Speaker assistant says: Certainly! Here are some additional tips for dealing with jet lag when traveling internationally:

1. Adjust your sleep schedule before you leave: Start adjusting your sleep schedule a few days before you leave so that it aligns with the time zone of your destination. This can help reduce the impact of jet lag once you arrive.

2. Stay hydrated: Dehydration can exacerbate the symptoms of jet lag, so be sure to drink plenty of water before, during, and after your flight.

3. Avoid alcohol and caffeine: Both alcohol and caffeine can disrupt your sleep, making it harder for you to adjust to the new time zone. Try to avoid them on your flight and in the days leading up to your trip.

4. Get some sunlight: Exposure to sunlight can help regulate your body clock and reduce the effects of jet lag. Try to spend some time outdoors during the day, especially in the morning.

5. Take a nap: If you arrive at your destination feeling tired, it can be helpful to take a short nap (no more than 20-30 minutes) to help you feel more alert and refreshed.

6. Use melatonin: Melatonin is a natural hormone that can help regulate your sleep-wake cycle. You can purchase melatonin supplements over-the-counter in most countries. However, you should consult with your doctor before taking them.

7. Give yourself time to adjust: Jet lag can take a few days to fully resolve, so be patient and give yourself time to adjust to the new time zone. Try to avoid scheduling important meetings or activities for the first day or two after you arrive.

Hopefully, these strategies will help you deal with jet lag and enjoy your international travels! context:Travel planning keywords: jet lag, sleep schedule, adaptation, travel tags: Travel, Frequent travelers

Here are some tips on how to start a travel blog that can help you build a loyal reader base and create a lucrative online business:

Choose a niche

The first step in starting a successful travel blog is to define your niche - this could be anything from budget travel to luxury travel to adventure travel to solo travel to family travel, and so on. By narrowing down your focus, you will be able to attract a specific target audience who are interested in your type of travel and create a unique brand identity.

Select a domain name and hosting

Once you have defined your niche, it's time to choose a catchy domain name that reflects your brand and is easy to remember. You can register a domain name and hosting through platforms such as GoDaddy or Bluehost. Ensure that your hosting provider offers reliable uptime, speedy site loading, and efficient customer support.

Choose a blogging platform

There are multiple blogging platforms available such as WordPress, Blogger, Wix, and Squarespace. Choose a platform that suits your needs and is user-friendly. WordPress is the most popular platform for bloggers due to its flexibility, customization options, and extensive plugin support.

Create compelling content

The most important aspect of a successful travel blog is the content. Create high-quality, engaging, and well-written posts that resonate with your readers. Share your travel stories, itineraries, tips, reviews, and insights to provide real value to your followers. Use high-quality images and videos to enhance your posts and make them more visually appealing.

Promote your blog

To attract visitors to your blog, you need to promote it effectively. Use social media platforms such as Instagram, Twitter, Facebook, and Pinterest to market your blog and engage with your audience. Join travel blogging communities and forums to network with other bloggers and gain exposure. Invest in SEO strategies such as keyword research, link building, and meta descriptions to improve your blog's visibility on search engines.

Monetize your blog

Once you have built a substantial readership, you can monetize your blog through various methods such as affiliate marketing, sponsored posts, advertising, and selling digital products such as e-books or courses. Remember, it takes time and effort to build a successful travel blog, but with dedication and perseverance, you can turn your passion into a profitable business.

content:Speaker assistant says: Certainly! Here are some effective communication strategies for managing online reputation during a crisis in Unit 3:
 
1. Act Fast
Timing is critical during a crisis. The longer it takes for an organization to respond, the more the crisis will escalate, and the harder it will be to manage. Therefore, you should act quickly, develop a plan, and implement it as soon as possible. Inform all necessary stakeholders immediately, including employees, the media, and customers.

2. Empathy and Acknowledgment
Acknowledge the crisis and express empathy and understanding towards those affected by it. Apologize for any harm caused sincerely. This gesture will go a long way in reassuring upset customers and helping to repair the organization's reputation.

3. Consistency in Messaging
Consistently communicate with all stakeholders and provide them with regular and truthful information regarding the crisis. Maintain the same message across all communication channels to avoid confusion or mixed-messages.

4. Transparency and Honesty
Demonstrate that the organization is transparent and honest with stakeholders. Keep all communication channels open by responding promptly to feedback and questions from affected parties.

5. Provide Actionable Steps
Provide actionable steps to manage the crisis and express what the company is doing or intend to do to resolve the issue as quickly as possible. Ensure that the stakeholders are aware of any steps that they need to take, such as who to contact, or what to do to minimize the impact of the crisis, thereby demonstrating that the organization is transparent and keen on providing solutions.

6. Monitor Online Conversations
Track, listen to, and engage with social media conversations. Company representatives should be available to answer any questions, address complaints, and dispel rumors as soon as the crisis starts. Responding correctly, honestly, and accurately is crucial during a crisis situation.

By following these communication strategies, organizations can manage their online reputation effectively during a crisis.
